title: Refactor and document as tutorial codebase
description: Add comprehensive documentation and light refactoring to make BeepFinder a teaching resource for an experienced developer learning the Android ecosystem. No behavior changes. Cover: AndroidManifest, Activity lifecycle, NotificationListenerService, Room ORM, Jetpack Compose + ViewModel, coroutines, foreground services, permissions, adaptive icons, Gradle/AGP. Add a README.md with architecture overview and guided code tour. Add inline comments to all source files.
close_reason: Full tutorial documentation pass complete. All 18 files documented. Build verified.

title: Investigate and fix notification flurry
description: Each audible notification on the phone results in multiple entries in BeepFinder. Need to diagnose why onNotificationPosted fires many times per beep — possible causes: system/internal notifications posted alongside the audible one, apps reposting/updating notifications (each update fires the callback), or service being bound multiple times. Fix the root cause so each user-visible beep produces a minimal number of entries.
close_reason: Fixed: skip FLAG_GROUP_SUMMARY, filter by channel importance, deduplicate same notification ID within 3s window.

title: Room database for notification history
description: Define NotificationEntity (id, timestamp, packageName, appLabel). Create NotificationDao with insert and query-last-24h methods. Set up NotificationDatabase as a singleton. Add a periodic pruning step to delete records older than 24 hours.
close_reason: Room DB implemented: NotificationEntity, NotificationDao, NotificationDatabase, NotificationRepository with 24h window and auto-pruning.

title: Implement NotificationListenerService
description: Create BeepListenerService extending NotificationListenerService. On each onNotificationPosted callback, extract the posting app package name and timestamp, resolve the human-readable app label, and persist to the Room database. Register the service in AndroidManifest.xml with the BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE permission.
close_reason: BeepListenerService implemented, registered in AndroidManifest with BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE permission.

title: Dev environment setup
description: Install Android Studio via brew, create initial Android project in the existing repo at ~/Documents/degel/beepfinder/ with Kotlin + Jetpack Compose template, package name com.degel.beepfinder, app name BeepFinder. Verify the project builds and runs on an emulator or device.
close_reason: Android Studio installed, SDK set up, project scaffolded, debug APK builds successfully.

title: Auto-start on device boot
description: BeepFinder currently only begins listening after the user manually opens the app post-reboot, creating a monitoring gap. Add a BroadcastReceiver listening for android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED (and QUICKBOOT_POWERON for some devices) that starts the service automatically. Requires RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission in the manifest. Works best in conjunction with the foreground service (beepfinder-4cd) — starting a foreground service from a boot receiver requires the app to call startForegroundService() and post the notification promptly.
close_reason: BootReceiver stub created and registered in manifest. NotificationListenerService is automatically rebound by Android after boot when permission is granted — no explicit start needed.

title: Run as foreground service with persistent notification
description: Promote BeepListenerService to a foreground service to prevent Android from killing it during extended idle periods. Requires posting a persistent notification, which can do double duty as the quick-glance display (see beepfinder-r5z): show the most recent notification source and time directly in the notification text, updating it each time a new entry is recorded. Implementation: call startForeground() in onListenerConnected with a NotificationChannel, update the notification content in onNotificationPosted. Tradeoff: permanent icon in status bar, but this is standard and expected for monitoring apps.
close_reason: startForeground() called in onListenerConnected with FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC. Persistent notification updated on each beep showing app name and time.

title: Battery optimization exemption prompt
description: Android's battery optimization (Doze mode) can kill BeepListenerService silently, causing gaps in the log. BeepFinder should detect if it is subject to battery optimization and prompt the user to exempt it. Approach: check PowerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations(packageName) on startup/resume; if not exempted, show a dismissible banner or dialog explaining the risk and offering a button that fires ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS to take the user directly to the exemption screen. Especially important on Pixel + Android 16 which has aggressive power management. Note: declaring REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS in the manifest requires justification in the Play Store permissions declaration.
close_reason: Dismissible warning banner shown when PowerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations() is false. Fix button fires ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS.

title: Service health indicator on main screen
description:
Show a status indicator on the main screen so the user knows whether BeepListenerService is actively listening. If Android kills the service (battery optimization, permission revoked, etc.) there would be silent gaps in the log with no visible warning.

**Realtime status:** Check both that notification access is granted (NotificationManagerCompat.getEnabledListenerPackages) and that the service is actually running (query ActivityManager or use a static flag on the service). Display a subtle 'Listening' or 'Service not running — tap to fix' indicator, with the latter linking back to Notification Access settings.

**Historic status:** Log service lifecycle events (onListenerConnected, onListenerDisconnected) to the Room database alongside notification entries, with a distinct entry type. Display these inline in the notification list as gap markers — e.g. 'Service stopped — 02:47' / 'Service resumed — 06:13' — so the user can tell whether a quiet period was genuinely quiet or a monitoring gap.
close_reason: Green/red dot in TopAppBar for realtime status. Service lifecycle events logged to DB and shown inline in the list as gap markers.

title: Only log audible notifications
description: Currently all notifications are logged regardless of whether they made a sound. Filter to only record notifications that actually triggered an audio alert. Approach: check the notification's channel importance (IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT or higher) and/or inspect the notification's sound/vibration flags via StatusBarNotification.getNotification(). May require looking up the NotificationChannel via NotificationManager to get the effective sound setting. This is core to the app's purpose and should be treated as medium priority.
close_reason: Fixed alongside flurry bug: isAudible() checks NotificationChannel.importance >= IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT.

title: Group repeated notifications in the UI
description: After the flurry bug is fixed, improve the list display by grouping consecutive or time-windowed entries from the same app. For example: 'WhatsApp — 10 times, last at 11:03' instead of 10 identical rows. Design should be informed by the real notification patterns observed after the flurry fix.
close_reason: Consecutive same-app entries merged into a single row with count badge and time range. Implemented via toGroups() in ViewModel layer.

title: Permission detection and onboarding screen
description: On launch, check if the app has Notification Access permission (NotificationManager.isNotificationListenerAccessGranted). If not, show a simple prompt explaining why the permission is needed with a button that deep-links to Settings > Notification Access. If granted, show the main list.
close_reason: Permission check in BeepFinderApp; PermissionPromptScreen with deep-link to Notification Access settings.

title: Main list UI (Jetpack Compose)
description: Simple full-screen list showing notification events from the last 24 hours, newest first. Each row shows: app icon (optional/nice-to-have), app name, and formatted timestamp. Use a LazyColumn. Data flows from Room via a ViewModel + StateFlow.
close_reason: NotificationListScreen (Compose LazyColumn) and NotificationViewModel implemented.

title: Start project
description: Interview the user to understand this project. Based on what you learn, create and organize beads
close_reason: Interviewed user. Project is a personal Android notification logger. Issues created and organized.

title: Show app icon in notification list
description: Display each app's icon alongside its name and timestamp in the list. PackageManager already provides the icon when we resolve the app label, so this is mostly a UI change. Makes the list faster to scan visually.
close_reason: AppIcon composable loads icon via PackageManager in a background coroutine (produceState). Displayed as 40dp image to the left of each notification group row.

title: Log notification sound URI per app
description:
Capture and display the sound associated with each notification, to help distinguish apps that use different alert tones. Scope: read NotificationChannel.getSound() at the time of onNotificationPosted to get the configured sound URI, and store it alongside the existing entry in the DB. Display the sound name (resolved from the URI) in the detail view or as a secondary line in the list row.

**Why this is the limit of what's feasible on Android:**
- NotificationListenerService has no access to the actual audio playback — only metadata
- Continuous mic recording for audio fingerprinting would be a privacy/permission/battery nightmare and would almost certainly be rejected by Play Store review
- AudioManager focus tracking around notification time gives no useful sound identity

**Difficulty:** Medium-hard. Sound URIs can be null (app uses default), can point to system sounds, app-internal resources, or arbitrary URIs. Resolving a human-readable name from an arbitrary URI is fiddly and may not always succeed. NotificationChannel lookup requires the channel ID from the notification, which is available but adds a layer of indirection.

**Priority note:** Nice-to-have only. Does not affect core functionality.
close_reason: NotificationChannel.getSound() captured; resolved via MediaStore query then last-path-segment fallback. Stored as soundLabel in DB (migration 2→3). Shown as '♪ name' in list row when non-null.

title: Dark mode support
description: Explicitly design for dark and light themes. Currently the app uses the default MaterialTheme without a custom color scheme, which may not look great in dark mode. Define a proper ColorScheme for both light and dark variants using Material 3's dynamic color or a hand-crafted palette, and apply it via a custom MaterialTheme wrapper. Should follow system setting automatically via isSystemInDarkTheme().
close_reason: BeepFinderTheme uses dynamicDark/LightColorScheme on API 31+, static Material 3 dark/light scheme as fallback. Follows system setting via isSystemInDarkTheme().

title: Play Store release preparation
description:
Tasks required before publishing BeepFinder on the Play Store:

1. **App icon** — Need adaptive icon (foreground + background layers) in mipmap-* densities plus mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml. Android Studio's Image Asset wizard can generate all sizes from an SVG.

2. **Signing keystore** — Generate a release keystore (keytool) and configure signingConfigs in app/build.gradle.kts. Store the keystore securely — losing it means you can never update the app on the Store.

3. **Release build** — Enable minification (isMinifyEnabled = true) and add a proguard-rules.pro file. Build with assembleRelease.

4. **Privacy policy** — Google requires a privacy policy for apps using NotificationListenerService. Must be hosted at a public URL. Policy must disclose that notification metadata is collected and stored locally only.

5. **Play Console setup** — Create app in Google Play Console (https://play.google.com/console), complete store listing (description, screenshots, content rating questionnaire).

6. **Sensitive permissions declaration** — NotificationListenerService requires filling out the Permissions Declaration Form in Play Console explaining the use case.

**Reference links:**
- Adaptive icons: https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/launch/icon_design_adaptive
- App signing: https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/app-signing
- Play Console: https://play.google.com/console
- Permissions declaration: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9214102
- NotificationListenerService policy requirements: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10208820

title: Configurable history retention length
description: 24-hour history window is currently hardcoded. Add a user-configurable setting (e.g. 24h / 3 days / 7 days) stored in DataStore. Surface this in the same settings screen as the per-app ignore/filter list (beepfinder-3mv). The Room query and pruning job in NotificationRepository both need to respect the configured window.
close_reason: Chip selector (24h/3d/7d) in Settings screen. Setting persisted in SharedPreferences; both DB query window and pruning respect it.

title: Per-app ignore/filter list
description: Allow the user to mute specific apps from appearing in the BeepFinder list. A settings screen shows all apps that have ever posted a notification (drawn from the DB), with a toggle to ignore each one. Ignored apps are still captured by the service but filtered out at the query or display layer. Useful for silencing noisy system apps or known non-interesting sources.
close_reason: Settings screen with toggle switches per app. Ignored packages stored in SharedPreferences, filtered in ViewModel. Apps drawn from current history window.

title: Quick-glance access without opening the app
description: Allow the user to see recent notification sources without launching BeepFinder. Two main options: (1) Persistent status bar notification — BeepFinderService posts/updates an ongoing notification showing the last 1-2 entries (e.g. 'Gmail, 11:03'); cheap to implement, always visible in the shade. (2) Home screen widget — a Glance (Jetpack) widget showing the recent list; more work but more flexible in size and layout. A third lighter option: (3) dynamic app shortcut or notification badge. Option 1 is simplest and probably sufficient for a personal-use app.
close_reason: Implemented as part of beepfinder-4cd: the foreground service notification updates its text to 'Last: AppName at HH:MM:SS' on every logged beep, providing quick-glance access from the notification shade without opening the app.
